user.title: ES Heat Pump – Credentials
user.description: Enter your myheatpump.com portal credentials. The integration logs in automatically and fetches all sensor data. For EU portal accounts, pick https://eu.myheatpump.com from the dropdown.

data.power_entity: Electrical-power sensor (optional, used for COP calculation)
data.energy_entity: Electricity meter of the heat pump (kWh, optional — more accurate than the power sensor)
data.mode_source_entity: Operating-mode source entity (no longer needed since v2.4.0 — the unit reports its mode in par1)
data.dhw_margin_k: Flow-temperature margin above the heating setpoint that marks DHW mode (K). Flow above setpoint + margin ⇒ domestic hot water.
data.flow_entity: Live volumetric-flow sensor (optional — overrides the constants, recommended if the circulation pump modulates)
data.model: Heat-pump model — selecting it fills in the datasheet nominal flow rate
data.enable_writes: Allow writing to the unit (off by default — required for settings entities, the restore service and parameter_setzen)
data.settings_interval: Configuration poll interval (seconds) — settings change rarely, 900 is plenty
data.backup_interval_h: Automatic backup interval (hours) — a change is always backed up immediately, this is the idle heartbeat
data.backup_keep: Number of backups to keep (0 = unlimited). Backups taken before a write or a restore are never deleted.

origami_theme_missing.title: Origami theme not installed
origami_theme_missing.description:
The ES Heatpump dashboard is set to the "Origami" design, but the theme "{theme}" is not installed. Until it is, Home Assistant shows the default theme.

To install: Marketplace/HACS → download the repository "hazymorning/origami" (category theme), then run the action "frontend.reload_themes" under Developer tools → Actions. The Montserrat font is optional, see the Origami README. This notice then disappears by itself.

cop_unplausibel.title: Implausible COP – check the flow rate
cop_unplausibel.description:
The current COP has been below 1 for several consecutive readings while the heat pump was running (last value: {cop}). That is physically impossible – the unit would deliver less heat than it draws in electricity.

Thermal power and COP are calculated from the configured flow rate (currently {volumenstrom} m³/h), which is almost certainly too low. Datasheet nominal value: {richtwert}.

Correct it in the integration options under "Measurement and calculation → Heating-loop flow rate" (or select your model). This notice disappears by itself as soon as the COP is plausible again.

cop_unplausibel_warmwasser.title: Implausible DHW COP – check the DHW flow rate
cop_unplausibel_warmwasser.description:
While heating domestic hot water, the current COP has been below 1 for several consecutive readings (last value: {cop}). That is physically impossible.

In DHW mode the thermal power is calculated from the configured DHW flow rate (currently {volumenstrom} m³/h), which is almost certainly too low. The built-in circulation pump P0 serves both the heating and the DHW circuit, so unless the controller display shows a different pump step for DHW, the DHW flow is about the same as the heating flow (currently {heizkreis} m³/h). Datasheet nominal value: {richtwert}.

Correct it in the integration options under "Measurement and calculation → DHW-loop flow rate". This notice disappears by itself as soon as the COP is plausible again.

sicherung_erstellen.description: Creates a backup of the complete configuration (about 300 values). Recommended before any change to the unit – and before every visit from the heating engineer.

sicherungen_auflisten.description: Returns all existing backups with time, occasion and checksum. Returns a response – fetch it in a script via "response_variable".

sicherung_anzeigen.description: Shows a backup in full – system data, all named settings in plain text and the raw values. Does not change anything on the unit.

sicherungen_vergleichen.description: Shows all differences between two states – by default between a backup and the current state of the unit. The response lists every changed value with name, group and plain-text value.

sicherung_wiederherstellen.name: Restore backup
sicherung_wiederherstellen.description: Writes a backed-up state back to the heat pump. By default as a dry run that only shows what would happen. A real run additionally requires write access to be enabled in the options, and automatically backs up the current state first.
